title: The positive FIN reduction case ends with the wrong membership sign.
details: Marks, version2024-02-25, Proposition17.5 proof, printed/PDF p.72. The positive case correctly proves that W_f(x) is finite, but its final displayed conclusion says x in A implies f(x) not in FIN. Replace the latter conclusion by f(x) in FIN. Indeed a witness y with all R(x,y,z) true is never enumerated, and the initial-segment guard prevents every larger number from entering; hence W_f(x) is a subset of {0,...,y-1}. If no witness exists, fairness and induction enumerate every number, giving an infinite set. This repairs the local sign without changing the reduction. Visually confirmed in the official PDF. The source version retains the sign slip. The corpus proves the corrected membership direction through an explicit prefix-refutation domain program.
